metadata.chapter_title: Map Projections and Coordinate Reference Systems
metadata.chapter_subtitle: Why every flat map distorts Earth, and how to choose coordinates that fit the question

inventory.summary: The foundations sequence had a genuine gap between introductory coordinates and later terrain or raster analysis. The new chapter was added to supply a direct explanation of CRS, datum, projection, and distortion tradeoffs.
issues: The core sequence lacked a dedicated chapter on map projections and coordinate reference systems.
Later chapters warned readers to check the CRS, but the conceptual foundation was missing.
The foundations arc needed an explicit bridge from coordinates to measurement-safe spatial analysis.

rewrite.summary: Drafted a full new foundations chapter that explains CRS choice in beginner-friendly language, ties it directly to later distance, area, and terrain calculations, and now uses dedicated visuals to show distortion and measurement tradeoffs.
editor_notes: Added a full chapter rather than a brief insert because the concept is foundational.
Kept the tone intuitive and avoided geodesy-heavy formalism.
Used worked examples and a selection checklist to connect theory to practice.

qa_review.summary: The chapter fills the missing conceptual bridge cleanly, defines notation on first use, and keeps the projection mathematics approachable for first-time readers.

repair.summary: The missing foundations topic was repaired by adding a new chapter and integrating it into the part sequence.
actions_taken: Added the new foundations chapter file.
Inserted the chapter into the book configuration and foundations index.
Renumbered the following terrain chapters to preserve sequence coherence.

design_review.summary: The chapter now combines worked examples, a practical checklist, and dedicated visuals so projection tradeoffs are shown rather than only described.
improvements_made: Added a selection checklist for choosing an appropriate CRS.
Included simple longitude-distance and projected-distance examples.
Added a radar visualization comparing what different projection choices preserve best.
Added named projection examples for Mercator, Sinusoidal, Albers equal-area conic, Lambert conformal conic, Polar stereographic, Azimuthal equidistant, and local projected grids.
Added a broader side-by-side graticule comparison so readers can see how several familiar projection families flatten the globe differently.
Added a Canada and Alberta decision example that ties projection choice to local distance work, provincial area comparison, and web-map display.
Added a western-Canada suitability chart to show why the best CRS depends on the task rather than on a single universal preference.
Added a latitude-versus-longitude-distance chart to show why degrees are not uniform measurement units.
Added a buffering-in-degrees chart to make projection error visible at a glance.
Positioned the chapter as an explicit bridge into later terrain and raster work.
